no_language: PODSHL has no {c} yet, so this window is in English. A language is one file — see spec/INTEGRATING.md.
intro_1: Describe your problem and tell me what is not working — a program, a device, a vendor. pip, NVIDIA, DATEV. I look up who publishes help for it, and what they need to know about this device.
intro_2: I read nothing, send nothing and change nothing without showing you first and asking.
intro_nollm: You have not set up your own model yet. When a vendor offers no agent — which today is the normal case — I cannot help you. Set one up, top right.
which_vendor_1: Type its name below — a program, a device or its maker: pip, NVIDIA, DATEV. I search the published catalogue on this device, so the search itself never leaves it.
which_vendor_2: Whoever publishes then says what to look at on your device — I do not have to guess in advance.
verified_1: This really is {v} — confirmed through a source the vendor does not control.
noagent_h: {v} does not publish a support agent
noagent_1: There is nobody there to ask ({r}). Today that is true of almost every vendor.
noagent_2: A vendor with an agent would now say what to look at on your device. Without one, your own model has to decide what matters.
needllm_h: Then I would need your own model
needllm_1: Without a vendor I answer using the model you set up yourself — local or cloud. Top right.
platform_note: That is what the agent knows about itself — nothing was read for it.
thinking_pick: {m} is working out what it needs to know …
thinking_pick_more: {m} is working out what else it needs …
pick_failed_h: The model could not choose anything
nothing_picked_h: The model did not want to look at anything
nothing_picked_1: It named neither a readable value nor a question.
questions_1: This appears in no command's output — only you know it.
declined_why: you did not have this, so it is sent as unanswered rather than left out
read_h: May I look at this on your device?
read_h_n: Round {n}: may I look at this as well?
read_own_cloud: {m} chose these values, and it does not run on this device. They leave your machine and go to the service behind it — not to us and not to {v}.
no_match_1: You picked one, the readings were taken, and the rules {v} wrote do not answer this combination. That is not a dead end — it is the case they have not covered yet.
none_fit_h: Then this is one {v} has not written down
none_fit_1: Nothing {v} published matches what you are seeing. That is worth them knowing: their answers only grow when somebody reports the case that was missing.
none_fit_2: A model can guess instead. It has not read this project and does not know it — treat anything it says as a guess, not as the project's answer.
unc_declined_h: Tell {v} that none of these is your problem?
unc_nomatch_h: Tell {v} that nothing they wrote answers this?
unc_declined_1: You looked at the problems {v} has written up and said none of them is the one in front of you. They cannot find that out any other way: asking their catalogue leaves no trace, and nobody opens an issue to say a support page was missing their case.
unc_nomatch_1: The readings were taken and the rules {v} wrote say nothing about this combination. They cannot find that out any other way: asking their catalogue leaves no trace, and the run simply ends.
unc_2: Anonymous and counted, like every report here. No timestamp, nothing that could identify you, and it is counted once per month however often you come back.
unc_nothing: Nothing about this device travels: nothing was read. What is sent is that somebody reached the end of what {v} published and found nothing.
unc_sent_h: Told — and now the text for you
unc_next: That was the count, and it carries no words. The rest of this page is a written-up report for their issue tracker, which you copy and paste yourself — nothing below leaves this machine on its own.
read_own: {m} chose these values. They go to your own model — not to us and not to {v}.
read_vendor: {v} needs {n} values for this. You decide item by item — whatever you withhold, I will ask you instead. Nothing is sent yet.
read_none_1: Nothing was read and nothing was sent.
read_done_note: None of it has left your device.
changed_1: Nobody publishes an answer for this, so there is no decision tree to walk — and this is the question that most often ends a diagnosis on its own. No tool can answer it.
changed_q: What changed shortly before this started?
changed_ph: an update, a driver, a setting, new hardware, a reinstall, a cable — or something you did differently
changed_nothing: nothing the user is aware of
ask_you_1_one: One thing only you can answer. You can fill it in or leave it blank.
ask_you_1_other: {n} things only you can answer. You can fill them in or leave them blank.
send_1: With these the vendor can say what is going on. Only this goes — nothing about you as a person.
edit_mine: Change what you wrote before it goes
edit_mine_1: These are your own words. What is shown is what will be sent — edit any of it, or empty a box to send nothing for that answer.
send_none_llm: Without these values {v} can say nothing. I can try your own model instead.
send_none_nollm: Without these values {v} can say nothing. You have not set up your own model yet.
no_skill_h: The vendor has nothing on file for this
no_skill_1: {r} I would hand this to a person.
finding_kb: The vendor's own instructions say otherwise
finding_kb_2: — that applies to other devices, not yours.
abstain_h: I would rather not answer that
changed_none_1: Everything on your device is as it was.
done_1: The setting is changed. A backup copy sits beside it — you can undo this at any time.
undone_1: The file is back in its original state.
repairs_h: A change made here wants another look
repairs_1: PODSHL changed something on this computer earlier, and something has moved since. Nothing was undone: whether the change is still needed is yours to decide.
repairs_ext_1: Another tool changed something on this computer and recorded it here, and something has moved since. Nothing was undone: whether the change is still needed is yours to decide.
repair_updated: The program was updated from {from} to {to} since the change.
repair_fixed: The publisher said {fixed} fixes the problem this change works around, and {now} is installed. The change may no longer be needed — or the fix may not have held.
repair_overwritten: The change is no longer in the file; something rewrote it.
repair_no_longer_set: The setting is no longer what the change set; something changed it back.
repair_file_changed: The file is no longer what it was after the change; something edited or replaced it.
repair_frozen: This package is held at {now} while the official one is now {avail}. Fixes and improvements since then are not reaching this computer.
repair_original_changed: What this local copy stands in front of has changed since the copy was made. The copy may now hide newer behaviour.
repair_pr_merged: The upstream fix is merged and not yet in a release.
repair_released_in: The upstream fix is in release {tag}.
repair_watch_note: Watching asks GitHub about this issue at most once a day. Each check tells GitHub which issue this computer follows.
repair_watching_note: This issue is watched: GitHub is asked about it at most once a day, and that tells GitHub which issue this computer follows.
repair_target_gone: The file the change was made in is gone.
repair_backup_gone: The copy an undo would restore is gone, so this change can no longer be undone here.
meth_if_wrong: What would show this is wrong
meth_measured: Rests on values read from this device: {f}
meth_supplied: Rests on what you said rather than on a measurement: {f}. If that was a guess, so is this.
followup_h: Anything missing, or do you know more?
followup_1: For example: which driver was installed, since when it happens, whether it is overclocked.
report_h: Report to {v} that this happened to you?
report_1: Voluntary, anonymous, and it helps: otherwise the vendor never sees how often this occurs.
report_2: No timestamp travels and nothing that could identify you.
contrib_1: Whether a vendor acts on reports is a figure no single vendor can compute — only many clients together. That is a separate transmission, so it is asked separately.
contrib_sep: Each vendor goes in its own request. The list of vendors you deal with is a picture of your installed software, and it is never sent as one piece.
receipt_h: Thank you — reply from the vendor
catch_h: Should {v} learn that this hit you?
catch_1: They have no agent, so they cannot help you. But we collect such cases and put them in front of them — free, confidential and unconditional.
catch_2: What is sent: the vendor's domain, the readings you consented to, and the size class of your model — plus a pseudonym that differs for every vendor and changes every month. No timestamp, no free text. The problem class is derived from the readings, not sent from here.
catch_ok_yes: This class has been reported by {n} independent reporters and will be put to {v}.
catch_ok_below: Recorded. Fewer than five independent people have reported this, so it is counted and not yet passed on — below five it would identify whoever did. How many is not shown here: counting up to the floor one report at a time is how the floor would be read from outside. Sending the same report again does not count.
llm_tip_none: Without your own model you get no answer when a vendor offers no agent. Click to set one up.
set_h: Model for when no vendor is reachable
set_1: You choose the provider and model. Local means the question never leaves your device. Cloud means it goes to your provider — not to us, but it does go.
set_key_note: The key is stored in the operating system's credential store, not in a file. Leave blank to keep the existing one.
set_key_have: Key stored — leave blank to keep it
set_loaded_one: One model available — it is filled in.
set_loaded_other: {n} models available — click the field to choose.
set_testing: Making a real request to the model …
set_saved_unreach: Saved. Not reachable yet — “Test connection” tells you why.
need_read: {v} would like to read one more thing:
need_again_h: The vendor keeps asking for the same thing
need_again_1: {v} has asked {n} times for something already answered, or already marked as unknown. It was told that, and the published rule is that it must not ask again — so this stops here rather than looping. Nothing further was sent.
esc_1: {r} — {v} takes the case, including what you typed.
esc_need: For that the vendor still needs:
esc_reply_h: How should the answer come back?
esc_human: A person decides — that is explicitly intended here.
vocab_h: What this agent is able to do at all
yours_1: Do you maintain something? Publish its support and anybody running it finds your answers here — a file in your repository, no server and no model of yours:
vocab_1: A vendor may only choose from this — it cannot bring a new capability.
reset_done: Reset. Your standing with every vendor starts over — in exchange nobody can link you to earlier reports.
notapplicable_h: This does not apply to this device
tr_failed: The vendor text is only available in English and your model could not translate it.
mismatch_1: You named {chosen}, but {found} was read from the device. I trust the machine over the memory.
model_done_1: Only you may end this. Keep looking, or answer now?
more_1: {m} still wants more after {n} rounds. You decide whether it continues.
set_incomplete: Both a provider and a model are needed.
env_1: On the search path I find {host}, but this project uses {project}.
proj_h: Is this about a project on disk?
proj_1: Then its folder lets me read the environment that project actually uses — its .venv, not whatever Python happens to be on the search path. I read files there; I run nothing. It lasts for this diagnosis only, and leaving it empty withdraws it.
proj_none: No folder — I will answer for this machine as a whole.
free_h: Send what you typed as well?
free_1: {v} asked these in their own words, and your answers stay here unless you say otherwise. An error message is usually the most useful thing they can get — and the one thing your machine cannot summarise for them.
free_2: Edit anything out that should not leave this device. What you see is exactly what is sent.
free_none_1: The report goes without it. Nothing you typed leaves this device.
free_ok_1: Your words go to {v} with the rest of the report.
pub_1: Which of these is your problem? These are the classes they said they can answer — picking one is better than us guessing which of your words maps to which of theirs.
pub_found_1: Published by {v}, from commit {c}. Matched against what was read on this device — no model was involved.
pub_supplied: This turned on {list}, which you told me rather than something I measured. If it is wrong, that may be why.
pub_none_1: That is not a verdict on them — they simply have not written this one down.
pub_unreach_h: The catalogue could not be reached
pub_unreach_1: {v} does publish answers for this. {o} holds them and did not answer, so they could not be fetched. Nothing about this machine was sent anywhere.
pub_unreach_2: That is a network failure, not a statement about the project. A name that resolves to the wrong address, a server being restarted — trying again is usually the whole of it.
pub_unreach_stopped_1: The published answers are still there and nothing was sent. Ask again when {o} is reachable — or ask the same question and choose “None of these”, which uses your own model instead.
loc_1: {d}: I would ask {p} itself — but it is not on this computer's search path. If it is installed, tell me where: the program file, or the folder it is in.
loc_2: I do not search your disk for it. Only this one program is started, with {f}, and only the version number it prints is kept. The location counts for this diagnosis only.
loc_empty: Enter the file or the folder first.
loc_noversion: {path} is {p}, but it did not name a version.
loc_none_h: {p} not read — the question stays open
log_hint: Usually in a file called {f}. Where it is on your machine, only you know — I do not search for it.
log_ph: Paste the lines around the error here — or load them below and delete everything else.
log_load: Load the end of this file
log_path_empty: Enter the path to the file first.
log_loaded_one: One line from {from}, shown only here. What you keep is anonymised and shown to you again before anything is sent.
log_loaded_other: {n} lines from {from}, shown only here. Keep the lines around the failure and delete the rest — what you keep is anonymised and shown to you again before anything is sent.
pub_try_1: Try their answer, then say. Whether it worked is what {v} most needs to know — and only you can tell them.
pub_report_1: Voluntary and anonymous. It goes to the maintainers of {v}, through the operator that mirrors their files — otherwise they never learn this happened, or whether their answer worked.
pub_dest: the maintainers of {v}, through the operator
pub_ok_yes: Recorded. {n} independent people have reported this, so {v} will see it on their dashboard.
pub_ok_below: Recorded. Fewer than five independent people have reported this, so it is counted and not yet shown to the maintainers — below five it would identify whoever did. How many is not shown here, for the same reason the floor exists.
pub_ok_again: You had already reported this this month, so it was not counted twice.
anon_done: Replaced before showing it to you: {list}.
anon_none: Nothing recognisable as personal was found — read it through anyway.
anon_cut: Cut to the last {n} lines ({c} characters at most).
lang_locked: The language stays as it is while a diagnosis runs — panels already on screen keep the words they were drawn with. It unlocks when this one ends.
stopped_1: You stopped this. Nothing further was read or sent — you can ask again.
finding_translating: Your model is translating the vendor's answer …
pub_send_1: The answers come from the files {v} publishes. {o} keeps a checked copy of those files and picks the answer that fits these values, so the values go to {o}. Nothing about you as a person goes with them. If one more thing is needed, I ask you and send that answer the same way.
pub_send_none_1: Nothing was sent to {o}. Without these values there is nothing to look up.
pub_english_no_model: This project writes in English, and you have no model of your own set up to translate it — its questions and its answer are shown as written.
set_test_cost: Makes one real request to the model. On a cloud provider that costs tokens.
set_test_saved: This tested the saved settings — save first to test what is in the form.
set_key_removed: The stored key is removed, and the settings are saved.
m_what_os_fact: A property of the operating system, read without running anything: {name}
m_what_run_tool: Run a system tool and read its output: {tool} {args}
m_what_read_file_key: The value “{key}” from the configuration file {path}
m_what_read_ini_key: The value “{key}” from the settings file {path}
m_what_enumerate_read: Search {root} for “{glob}” and read {keys} from what is found (at most {max} entries)
m_what_program_version: Run {path} {flag} and keep only the version number it prints
m_what_program_version_absent: {program} is not on this computer's search path — you will be asked where it is, and only that one program is started, with {flag}
m_what_container_image_version: Ask Docker which version of the image {image} is running — read from docker ps; nothing runs inside the container
pub_report_h: Tell the maintainers of {v} that this happened to you?
refused_system: belongs to the operating system and is never run for a version
refused_outside: outside what this client may read
refused_invalid: not a reading this client performs
pseudo_explain: A different value for every recipient, and a new one every month. The recipient can count and block, but cannot recognise you across recipients or across months.
att_live: Control of {h} was confirmed on {d} — that is what is attested: who controls the location, not whether the advice is right.
att_stale: Control of {h} was last confirmed on {d}, more than two weeks ago. Their files are still served; they may no longer be maintained.
att_unknown: Nobody has confirmed control of {h} recently. Treat this as a stranger's advice.
att_log: Recorded in the public log as entry {n}, so anybody can check what was served.
att_deprecated: The project itself says it is deprecated.
att_deprecated_to: The project itself says it is deprecated, in favour of {s}.
att_archived: Its repository is archived by its owner.
loc_err_wrong_name: That file is not {p}. Only the program that was asked about is started.
loc_err_system: That file belongs to the operating system and is never started for a version.
loc_err_denied: That program is never started for a version, whatever anybody clicks.
loc_err_empty: Enter the file or the folder first.
loc_err_not_in_folder: There is no program called {p} in that folder.
loc_err_not_executable: That is not a program file, or it does not exist.
log_err_no_docker: Docker is not available on this device.
log_err_denied: That file is barred, whatever anybody clicks.
log_err_unreadable: That file could not be read — check the path.
q_pattern: The highlighted answer does not have the form the publisher asked for.
env_why: The Python on the search path is not the one this project uses.
att_checking: Checking the log on this device …
att_proved: Checked on this device: the entry is in the signed log of {n} entries, and it vouches for exactly these files.
att_unproved: This device could not confirm that entry in the signed log — nobody vouches for these files right now.
m_no_answer_in_time: no answer within the time limit
m_no_card_at_well_known: no Agent Card at the well-known URI
m_not_a_card: the answer is not an Agent Card
m_action_unknown: unknown action {id} — this client knows {known}. A vendor may only choose from these.
m_params_not_object: the parameters are not an object
m_dry_report_only: States a finding. Nothing on this device is changed.
m_dry_set_config_key: Sets {key} = {value} in {file} — a .bak copy is kept.
m_path_leaves_root_named: the path leaves the root folder: {p}
m_path_leaves_root: the path leaves the root folder
m_no_backup: There is no backup copy — nothing to undo.
m_denied_even_with_consent: refused: {d} is barred, and stays barred with consent
m_program_never_run: {p} is never run, not even for its version — it starts other programs, changes the state of the machine or alters data rather than naming a version
m_no_program_in_folder: There is no program called {p} in {dir}
m_wrong_program_name: The file is called {name}, and the question is about {p}. Only the program that was asked about is run.
m_system_program: {p} belongs to the operating system and is not run for a version
m_read_no_op: a read instruction without an op
m_read_op_unknown: unknown read instruction {op} — this client does not perform it
m_what_run_tool_bare: Run a system tool and read its output: {tool}
m_not_ascii: {field} {v} is not ASCII — a name that only looks like an allowed one is exactly the evasion the deny list exists to stop
m_tool_not_allowed: the tool {tool} is not on the allow list {known}
m_tool_absent: {tool} is not available on this device — this reading cannot be taken here.
m_arg_not_allowed: the argument {a} is not permitted for {tool}
m_gpu_field_identifying: {field} names which card this is rather than describing it, and is not read whoever asks
m_registry_name_identifying: {name} names this machine or its owner rather than what is installed on it, and is not read whoever asks
m_env_var_not_allowed: {name} is not one of the environment variables a diagnosis may read — those are {allowed}. The environment is where exported passwords live, so this is a list of what may be read rather than a list of what may not.
m_path_backstep: the path contains a step back (..) and so leaves the permitted area: {p}
m_path_relative_no_project: {p} is relative to the project folder, and none has been granted for this diagnosis
m_path_outside: the path is outside the permitted configuration areas: {p}
m_program_not_allowed: the program {p} is not permitted — a bare name only, never a path
m_flag_not_allowed: the argument {flag} is not permitted — possible are {allowed}
m_image_not_allowed: the image {image} is not permitted — a repository name without a tag only
m_glob_path_change: a search pattern may not change directory
m_root_unknown: unknown root {root} — permitted are config, data
m_cat_os_container: Is this running in a container?
m_cat_python_venv_version: Python version of the project environment (.venv)
m_cat_python_venv_base: The interpreter the project environment was created from
m_cat_pip_version: Version of the pip package manager
m_cat_agent_default: Which coding agent this desktop uses
m_log_changed_identity: The log is signed by a different key than the one this device checked before ({was} → {now}). That is another log, not a change to this one — nothing relates the two.
m_log_shrank: The public log is smaller than when this device last checked it ({was} entries, now {now}). A log that loses entries has been rewritten. If you reset the server yourself, remove log_seen.json to start the chain again.
m_log_forked: The log reports the same size as before ({size} entries) with a different content. One of the two was never the real log.
m_log_not_an_extension: The log cannot show that it grew from what this device saw before ({was} entries, now {now}). Entries have been changed or removed. If you reset the server yourself, remove log_seen.json to start the chain again.
m_answer_unreadable: the answer could not be read: {e}
m_answer_too_large: the answer is larger than {max} bytes and was not read to the end
m_https_required: {host} is not on this machine and was addressed without encryption. The readings would travel in clear text to anyone on the way, so nothing is sent.
m_card_unsigned: The Agent Card is not signed
m_no_oob_key: No out-of-band key for {host} via {source} — a self-asserted Agent Card is not accepted.
m_skill_malformed: The skill does not match the published format: {e}
m_finding_malformed: The finding does not match the published format: {e}
m_finding_not_for_this_request: The finding is signed, and it is not the answer to this request about {skill}. It may be an answer to another question, or an older one sent again.
m_facts_not_canonical: the readings could not be brought into their canonical form, so the answer cannot be bound to them: {e}
m_report_malformed: The report does not match the published format: {e}
m_too_many_reads: This flow wants to read {n} values. More than {max} is no longer a diagnosis.
m_channel_email: An answer by email to the address given
m_channel_ticket_url: Status available at any time at a case address
m_channel_none: No reply — the vendor says so explicitly
m_reply_channel_unknown: The reply channel {via} is not supported by this client — possible are {known}.
anchor_repo: a repository on {f} — the forge decides who may write there
anchor_domain: a domain — DNS and TLS say who served this
prov_h: Check where this machine got it from?
prov_1: PODSHL can ask your package manager which project it installed {s} from, and compare that with the one you picked. Nothing is sent anywhere.
prov_warn: Your system says {s} came from {d} ({src}), not from {p}. That happens honestly — a fork, a repackaged version — but it is worth a look before you trust an answer.
issue_1: Everything you were asked and everything this machine read, as Markdown for an issue. It is anonymised the same way a report is — and this one is more public, so read it before you paste it.
issue_where: The project asks for issues at {d}.
issue_en: It is in English: every project here publishes English, so that is the language a maintainer can certainly read. Your own words are exactly as you wrote them.
issue_footer: Add a line saying PODSHL assembled it
issue_unstated: Not measured here: {list}. {n} in the answer and this machine did not report {n2} — worth checking before a maintainer goes looking.
nodir_h: The published directory could not be checked
nodir_1: This client holds no directory it could verify, so it is not using one — an unchecked directory is worse than none. Until that is fixed, no published project can be found by name, whatever it publishes.
nodir_2: Usually this means the client was built without the operator's public log key, or the operator could not be reached when it last tried.
nodir_3: The directory was checked and holds {n} project(s) — this one is in it, but with no answers of its own.
m_how_known_vendor: from the list of known vendors
m_how_guessed: guessed from the name — please check
m_index_no_pinned_key: no pinned log key — an unchecked index is not used
m_index_entry_unproven: {host} is in the index but cannot be shown to be in the log
m_index_unreadable: The index could not be read: {e}
m_secret_unreadable: The client secret cannot be read: {e}
m_secret_uncreatable: The client secret cannot be created: {e}
m_secret_wrong_length: The client secret has the wrong length
m_key_source_pinned: the pinned file {p} (a stand-in for an ANS/DNS lookup)
m_key_source_dns: DNS TXT via the Agent Name Service
m_report_bad_outcome: The outcome {o} is not one a report can carry
m_free_text_without_consent: Free text is not sent without its own consent naming a recipient
m_free_text_too_long: more than {n} characters of free text
m_consent_without_recipient: Consent without a named recipient is not consent
m_signature_unreadable: the signature could not be read: {e}
m_log_no_pinned_key: no pinned log key — nothing is claimed unchecked
m_sth_signature_invalid: The tree head signature is invalid: {e}
m_entry_beyond_head: entry {seq} lies beyond the signed head ({size})
m_proof_wrong_size: a proof for a different tree size than the signed head
m_entry_not_in_log: entry {seq} is not in the signed log of size {size}
m_entry_attests_other: entry {seq} attests {field} {got}, and what is served is {want}
m_guide_other_os: These instructions are for {want}; this device runs {os}.
m_standing_network: {v}: {pct} % of reports answered (median of {n} independent clients, range {lo}–{hi} %).
m_standing_not_offered: The report is not offered — it would be wasted effort.
m_standing_too_few: {v}: too few reports yet to say anything.
m_standing_rate_low: {v} has ever acted on {pct} % of reports.
m_no_model: No model of your own is set up.
m_translation_unreadable: The translation could not be read: {e}
m_log_source_unknown: The source {source} is not permitted — possible are container, file
m_repair_cli_notify: {n} recorded local fixes want another look. Open PODSHL, or run: podshl-client repairs review
m_repair_cli_notify_one: One recorded local fix wants another look. Open PODSHL, or run: podshl-client repairs review
m_repair_cli_show_watched: asked of GitHub at most once a day (watching is on)
m_repair_cli_show_not_watched: not asked of GitHub (switch it on: podshl-repairs watch {id} on)
m_repair_cli_show_no_copy: no copy to go back to
m_repair_cli_retired_silent: the package no longer declares this
m_repair_cli_declarer_gone: the package that declared this is no longer installed
repair_retired_silent: The package no longer declares this.
repair_declarer_gone: The package that declared this is no longer installed.
m_repair_cli_notify_run: {n} recorded local fixes want another look. Run: {cmd}
m_repair_cli_notify_run_one: One recorded local fix wants another look. Run: {cmd}
m_repair_cli_heading: PODSHL — recorded local fixes that want another look:
m_repair_forget_needs_root: Removing a record needs administrator rights. The tools this record keeps track of run as you do, so removing one is deliberately not something they can do: start an administrator terminal (or use sudo) and try again.
m_repair_forget_needs_a_person: Removing a record needs somebody to answer here, and nothing is reading this terminal. Run it where you can type.
m_repair_forget_what_goes: What this record says goes, and the copy it kept goes with it. A stub stays, saying a record existed and was removed.
m_repair_forget_confirm: Type the record id to remove it ({id}), or anything else to stop:
m_repair_forget_not_confirmed: That is not the record's id. Nothing was removed.
m_repair_forgotten: Removed: {id}. A stub stays, saying a record existed and was removed.
m_repair_cli_forgotten_row: removed; what it said is gone
m_repair_cli_updated: updated from {from} to {to} since the fix
m_repair_cli_fixed: upstream says {f} has the fix, and {i} is installed
m_repair_cli_overwritten: the setting is no longer in the file
m_repair_cli_no_longer_set: the setting is no longer what the fix set
m_repair_cli_backup_gone: the copy to go back to is gone
m_repair_cli_file_changed: the file changed since the fix
m_repair_cli_frozen: held at {i}, the official package is now {a}
m_repair_cli_original_changed: what this copy overrides has changed
m_repair_cli_pr_merged: the upstream fix is merged, not yet released
m_repair_cli_released_in: the upstream fix is in release {t}
m_repair_external_bad: The change cannot be recorded: {k} is missing or not in the expected form.
m_repair_external_path: The change cannot be recorded: {p} does not exist.
m_repair_no_issue_to_watch: Only a GitHub issue or pull request link can be watched.
m_dry_restart_service: Restart the Windows service {s}. Windows will ask for administrator permission first. There is nothing to undo: the service is stopped and started again.
m_dry_set_service_start: Set the Windows service {s} to start as "{start}". Windows will ask for administrator permission first. The current setting is kept, so this can be undone.
m_dry_set_machine_env: Set the machine-wide environment variable {n} to {v}. Windows will ask for administrator permission first. The current value is kept, so this can be undone; programs started from now on see the new one.
m_dry_unset_machine_env: Remove the machine-wide environment variable {n}. Windows will ask for administrator permission first. The current value is kept, so this can be undone.
m_elevated_protected: {id} is refused: Windows needs what it would change to run, update or protect itself.
m_elevated_refused: {id} is refused: its parameters are not in the form administrator actions accept.
m_elevated_windows_only: {id} needs administrator rights and is only available on Windows so far.
m_elevated_not_found: {id}: what it would change does not exist on this computer.
m_elevated_helper_missing: The program that makes administrator changes ({h}) is not installed next to PODSHL, so nothing was changed.
m_elevated_declined: Administrator permission was not given, so nothing was changed.
m_elevated_denied: Windows did not allow the change, so nothing was changed.
m_elevated_timed_out: The change did not finish in time. Check the state before trying again.
m_elevated_start_type: This service is started by Windows itself at boot, and these changes do not touch such services.
m_elevated_not_applied: The helper reported success, but reading the computer again does not show the change, so it is not recorded as made.
m_repair_upstream_bad: What the publisher says about the software is not usable: {k} is not in the expected form.
m_repair_not_written: The record of this change could not be written, so nothing was changed: {e}
m_repair_not_installed: The package manager does not know {p}, so its version cannot be compared.
m_repair_vcs: {v} is a build from a repository's head; no release number is before or after it.
m_repair_unknown: There is no record of that change.
m_published_loading: The operator is still reading {host}'s published files. Try again in a minute.
m_published_cannot_check: The operator cannot read {host}'s published files right now, so it answers nothing from them. That says nothing about the project.
m_published_cannot_use: {host}'s current published files were not accepted, so the operator answers nothing from them until they are. Its maintainer is told why.
m_no_container_of: No container of the image {image} is running
act_set_config_key: Set a key in a configuration file
m_free_text_over: {n} characters is more than the {max} of free text a report carries — cut it down to the lines around the error
pub_translated: Machine-translated by your own model — the answer itself was found without one. The original is one click away, top right.
pub_terms_lost: While translating, your model changed words that had to stay as the project wrote them: {list}. Before you run a command, check the original — one click away, top right.
pub_translating: Your model is translating what the project wrote …
pub_tr_failed: The project writes in English and your model could not translate it — it is shown here as written.
vendor_translating: {v} does not serve this language — your model is translating …
devbuild_why: Built without an operator or a pinned log key, so it talks to {o} and cannot verify a published directory. Build it with scripts/build/build_client.sh or build_client.ps1.
